metadata.title: #432 The Mind of Napoleon
metadata.guest_role: Solo biography (Napoleon / J. Christopher Herold ed.)

conclusion: Senra's second Napoleon tape is Herold's 1955 The Mind of Napoleon — about 300 pages of the man talking. Destiny is the doctrine: sacrifice comfort and happiness; every thought is a step to action. Luck is exploiting accidents, not chance. Men move by fear and self-interest. Success makes the great man. He dictated army bulletins himself and 21 sheets for Josephine's water-cure. Founders after World War II still study him the way they later study Churchill. This is a methods tape, not a Waterloo chronology.
background: Follow-on to episode 294 (Napoleon: A Concise Biography, 130–140 pages). Senra wants the primary voice: Lauren Powell Jobs' line that the best way to understand someone is to listen to them. Pre-WWII founders kept rereading Napoleon; after the war Churchill joins the shelf. Themes: destiny, will, propaganda, contradictions dated by year.
important_facts: Book and doctrine: first published 1955, ~300 pages grouped by theme, Napoleon speaking. Chief doctrine, repeated: sacrifice comfort, self-interest, and happiness to destiny; destiny must be fulfilled. Work is his element — he has known the limits of his legs and eyes, never of working capacity. Inaction is unbearable. Luck is a consecutive series of great actions, the ability to exploit accidents; shallow men believe in luck, strong men in cause and effect (Emerson). Andreessen's malleable-world line from episode 50 is the modern rhyme. Immortality: to live without glory, without a trace, is not to have lived. Men of genius are meteors consumed lighting their century.

Psychology and method: men are moved by two levers, fear and self-interest — the advertising founders (Lasker, Hopkins, Ogilvy) later sell the same way. Start by believing the worst; people would have to be exceptional rascals to match his assumption (Munger/Cicero cynicism; episode 286). His wife could have died and it would not have interrupted plans for a quarter of an hour. Suicide is a Monday-night mood that steals Saturday. 'It is success which makes the great man' — Britain had to recognize Washington because he won. All great events hang by a single thread; the less clever man neglects one thing and misses everything (LBJ: if you do everything you will win). Imagination rules the world. Senra's Readwise pile is 20,000+ highlights; he keeps tying this book to episode 214 (Isaacson/Jobs), 251 (Franklin/Washington, 250–300 pages), and 299 (Jobs archive).

Propaganda and contradiction: 1806 he wants no book censorship; a footnote says in 1810 he established it. He informs the Pope he can depose him as predecessors did. 'The masses must be guided without their noticing it' — ink and paper. He dictated all important army bulletins to inform, counter rumor, mislead the enemy, and stir enthusiasm; he was his own minister of propaganda. When shaved he skipped French papers: they only say what he tells them. The art of ruling is making others work — then he dictates 21 large sheets for Josephine's water-cure itinerary. Jobs came back to Apple and sat a long Wednesday three-hour marketing meeting because great products still need a great marketing company; Senra's read of Insanely Simple is that no Missouri billboard shipped without Steve. Same instinct, different stakes.

mental_model.name: Destiny Then Action × Own Propaganda × Dated Contradictions
mental_model.components: First name the destiny, then spend the thought as a step to an act. Treat luck as exploited accidents. Move people with fear and self-interest, not product features. Success, not permission, makes the great man — Washington vs Britain. Do the communications yourself: bulletins, Wednesday marketing, every external page. Expect hypocrisy; Herold dates the quotes so 1806 no-censorship sits next to 1810 censorship. Micromanage the message; try not to dictate 21 sheets of spa itinerary. Study the man in his own words (294 for the life, 432 for the mind).
mental_model.application: AAPL is the Jobs rhyme Senra keeps pressing — own the marketing meeting, ship no billboard you have not seen. BRK.B is the Buffett/Munger shelf this tape keeps opening (opportunity-driven, cynicism about human nature, do not go where you will die). Private:Napoleon is the methods object, not a security. Fade founders who wait for luck or outsource the story. Do not copy unlimited-power information control as a product strategy; copy the 'do it yourself' part. A quote without a year is how you miss the contradiction.

key_insights.question: What is the doctrine?
key_insights.answer: Find the destiny, then act. Work has no known limit. Inaction is the thing he cannot bear.

key_insights.question: Why did Britain recognize Washington?
key_insights.answer: Because he won. Permission follows the result. Imagination rules; plans stay as projects.

key_insights.view: Be your own minister of propaganda.
key_insights.question: Who writes the bulletin?
key_insights.answer: Napoleon dictated them. Jobs took Wednesday. French papers only said what he told them.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Jobs-as-own-marketer is the operator print Senra maps onto Napoleon; not a new iPhone thesis — low
Buffett/Munger cynicism and opportunity-driven lines are the living shelf, not a 1800s replay — low
